pharm: Potent direct-acting cholinergic agonist used in ophthalmology; intraocular 0.01% solution to induce miosis during surgery and topical solutions to lower intraocular pressure in glaucoma.
quick: Intraocular: up to 0.5 mL of 0.01% into anterior chamber
Use only if benefit justifies fetal risk
summary: Carbachol is a potent cholinergic (parasympathomimetic) agent used in ophthalmology. The intraocular 0.01% solution (Miostat) is instilled into the anterior chamber to produce miosis during cataract and other ocular surgery and to reduce postoperative intraocular pressure rise; topical solutions (0.75-3%) are used to lower intraocular pressure in glaucoma. It produces pupillary constriction within minutes by stimulating cholinergic receptors of the iris sphincter.
indications: Intraocular use to obtain miosis during ocular (e.g., cataract) surgery
Reduction of elevated intraocular pressure in the first 24 hours after cataract surgery
Topical treatment of open-angle and certain other glaucomas to lower intraocular pressure (topical formulations)

dosage.d: No more than 0.5 mL of 0.01% solution
dosage.t: Single dose, gently instilled before or after securing sutures
dosage.n: Miosis usually maximal within 2-5 minutes; single-dose use only, discard remainder
Topical formulations only; titrate concentration/frequency to IOP response

admin: Intraocular: instill no more than 0.5 mL into the anterior chamber using an atraumatic cannula; for single intraocular use only - discard any unused portion
Topical: instill drops into the conjunctival sac; apply nasolacrimal occlusion to reduce systemic absorption
Do not touch the dropper/cannula tip to the eye or other surfaces
Note the vial stopper may contain latex (allergy risk)
Wash hands before and after use
moa: Carbachol is a potent cholinergic (parasympathomimetic) agonist that stimulates muscarinic (and some nicotinic) receptors; it contracts the iris sphincter producing miosis and contracts the ciliary muscle, which increases aqueous humor outflow and reduces intraocular pressure. Unlike acetylcholine it resists cholinesterase, giving a longer action.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to carbachol or any component of the preparation
Acute iritis and other conditions where miosis/cholinergic stimulation is undesirable

preg: Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether carbachol is excreted in human milk; exercise caution in nursing mothers.
renal: Not applicable; ophthalmic use with minimal systemic exposure.
hepatic: Not applicable; ophthalmic use with minimal systemic exposure.

moderate: Topical beta-blockers and other antiglaucoma agents (additive IOP-lowering)
minor: Topical NSAIDs (theoretical reduction of miotic effect via prostaglandin pathway)

rare: Systemic cholinergic effects (flushing, sweating, abdominal cramps, vomiting, salivation, bradycardia)
emergency: Retinal detachment with acute vision loss

monitoring: Degree and adequacy of miosis (intraoperatively, within 2-5 minutes)
Systemic cholinergic signs in susceptible patients
counsel: Your vision may be temporarily blurred and dim, especially at night or in low light - avoid driving until vision clears
A brief stinging sensation or brow ache may occur
For drops, press gently on the inner corner of the eye for a minute after instillation to reduce body absorption
Tell your eye doctor about asthma, heart disease, ulcers, thyroid problems, or latex allergy
Do not touch the dropper tip to your eye
pk: Miosis within minutes; intraocular maximal at 2-5 min
Intraocular miosis ~24 hours; topical IOP effect several hours
Store as labeled (typically room temperature); protect from light
pearls: Resists cholinesterase, so its action is longer than acetylcholine - useful for sustained surgical miosis
Intraocular 0.01% (Miostat) is for single intraocular use only - discard the unused portion
Use cautiously in asthma, peptic ulcer, bradycardia, hyperthyroidism, and urinary obstruction due to systemic cholinergic effects
missed: For surgical intraocular use this is a single intraoperative dose with no missed-dose concept. For topical glaucoma drops, instill the missed dose when remembered unless near the next dose; do not double.
overdose: Excess produces systemic cholinergic toxicity (salivation, sweating, bradycardia, hypotension, bronchospasm, GI cramps). Treat with atropine (the specific antidote) and supportive care; provide respiratory support if needed.
